import pandas as pd

# In pandas 3.0.0, Copy-on-Write is the default behavior
df = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1, 2, 3]})
view = df['A']
view.iloc[0] = 999
# In 3.0.0, this does NOT modify the original due to CoW
assert df['A'].iloc[0] == 1, "Expected CoW to prevent modification"
entries.before:
import pandas as pd

# In pandas 2.3.3, the default mode allows copy-on-write to be disabled
df = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1, 2, 3]})
view = df['A']
view.iloc[0] = 999
# In 2.3.3, this modifies the original by default (unless CoW is explicitly enabled)
assert df['A'].iloc[0] == 999, "Expected modification to propagate in 2.3.3"
entries.title: Copy-on-Write (CoW) enabled by default changes Series copy behavior

entries.before:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# In pandas 2.x, object dtype Series.values returns numpy array of objects
s = pd.Series(['a','b','c'])
# Check the old object dtype is returned
assert s.values.dtype == np.dtype('O'), f'Expected object dtype, got {s.values.dtype}'
entries.title: DataFrame.to_numpy with dtype parameter: object dtype inference changed for string-typed DataFrames

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# In pandas 2.3.3, Series.argmax(skipna=False) with NaN returns index position
